workingPapers.title: Portable Checkpoints Can Reduce Completion
workingPapers.abstract: We study a procurement contract in which the incumbent privately learns its opportunity cost of completion after delivering an intermediate output that a replacement can use. Greater replacement availability raises expected surplus but can lower the probability of completion. The buyer reduces the incumbent's completion bonus, inducing exit by marginal types before replacement availability is known. If availability is observed and contractible before the exit decision, completion is increasing in replacement availability.

notes.title: What could we do with spare AI time?
notes.summary: A market could put spare AI usage to work. The first model asks how the prospect of a backup changes the incentive to finish a task.
